title: First contact: SDK Hyperdrive playbook (90m lab) - sketch
summary: A lightweight, hands-on 90 minute lab to take a new integrator from signup to a working sample app calling Redwood (text + streaming) with basic telemetry and a fallback test. Focus on friction removal, measurable checkpoints, and explicit failure-mode practice.
content:
Purpose
---
Quick internal sketch for a compact, instructor-led "90 minute" workshop that doubles as a self-serve quickstart. Target is devs/engineers who want a real integration (not a toy): call generation + streaming, handle errors, validate cost/latency signals, and run a canary fallback.

Audience / persona
---
- Primary: product engineers integrating Redwood for a feature (chat, summarization, retrieval).
- Secondary: platform/product PMs who want to evaluate run costs and rollback patterns.

High-level goals (measurable)
---
- Developer has working sample app calling Redwood API end-to-end in <= 60 minutes.
- App shows streaming UI + token-level latency bar.
- Telemetry: per-request tokens, model, latency, error class sent to SDK shim.
- Failure drill: simulate region outage and exercise automatic fallback to cheaper model/region in <= 10 minutes.

Logistics / formats
---
- Formats: instructor session (remote or in-person) OR self-serve repo with a single command: ./hyperdrive-start (shell + Docker).
- Languages: Node (primary), Python (secondary). Keep code samples to <= 40 LOC for core flows.

90-minute instructor timeline (tight)
---
0-10m: intro + expected outcomes + quick account setup notes (api key + billing check).
10-30m: scaffold repo, run local server, wire SDK client, make initial text generation call (non-streaming) — confirm tokens & response.
30-50m: switch to streaming endpoint, wire incremental UI (simple text area + appended tokens). Show token-level latency timing.
50-65m: add telemetry hooks (send token count, latency, model selection to the shim). Walk through sample dashboard screenshot.
65-75m: introduce a model routing policy; show how to configure a fallback model in config.yaml.
75-85m: failure drill — use a script to block primary endpoint and observe automatic fallback; walk through log traces.
85-90m: wrap, next steps, repo pointers, feedback link.

Preflight checklist (instructor & repo)
---
- repo contains: docker-compose, env.example, simple UI, server shim that proxies to Redwood SDK.
- ./hyperdrive-start validates API key and prints quick health: models available, quota status.
- sample prompts and golden responses for smoke tests (to validate output format).

Core code patterns to highlight
---
- Idempotent request IDs (X-Request-Id) so retries are observable in tracing.
- Short-circuit on partial stream: show how to cancel/trim KV-cache usage to keep latency.
- Small batch vs single-token tradeoff: show config presets (latency-first, cost-first) and measured token/sec.

Telemetry + observability (practical)
---
- Minimum signals to capture: model.name, model.variant, request_id, user_id (hashed), prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, response_latency_ms, error_type.
- Implement a shim that emits to console + a local file used by instructor to show live-sourced dashboards (Grafana-lite or simple web endpoint).
- Show a canonical trace example (single span for request, sub span for streaming loop).

Failure modes & exercises
---
- Simulated high-latency: insert artificial 500ms delay in runtime shim and have the team flip to latency-first preset.
- Simulated quota rejection: mock 429 and show graceful UI error + exponential backoff in the client.
- Region outage: block host and confirm fallback to alternate region/model variant via routing policy.

Student troubleshooting cheats
---
- blank responses: check API key scope & chosen model (rare if model incorrectly pinned).
- streaming stalls: confirm chunked transfer encoding headers + verify client SSE/WS handling.
- token ballooning: inspect prompt construction for accidental loops or long context.

Safety and policy notes (quick)
---
- Remind students that this is a lab using public models; any customer data must be scrubbed.
- Provide a short doc link to our data handling and private deployment options (private deployments example commands included in repo).

Example config snippets (human readable)
---
- config.yaml presets: latency-first, cost-first, balanced. Each preset maps to max_batch_size, kv_cache_enabled, quantization_profile.
- routing policy example: primary: hosted-us-west, fallback: hosted-europe, model-override: small-quantized when latency>200ms.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Do we bundle a lightweight eval harness so students can run a prompt-regression test after changing presets? (ideally yes — helps drive Optimize product.)
- Should the starter repo include both progressive disclosure (start minimal then add features) and a single-command full-run? Which path is the canonical onboarding?
- Add a one-page cheat sheet for non-engineers (PMs) summarizing cost/latency tradeoffs.

Notes to self (informal)
---
- Keep Node server under 200 LOC and keep plumbing explicit for teaching.
- Make the streaming UI intentionally ugly — focus on correctness and observability, not CSS.
- Reuse existing telemetry events contract if possible (ask SRE for current schema).

Next steps (this doc)
---
- Prototype the repo skeleton and attach to this doc (owner: Priya).
- Run a dry-run with Solutions Eng on 2025-02-12 (tentative).
- Create a small PR template for contributors with a 'smoke test' checklist.

Appendix: sample prompts (for golden smoke tests)
---
- "Summarize this support ticket in 2 lines and list three actions the engineer should take."
- "Given the following changelog excerpt, propose a short release note blurb."

End of sketch.

(Informal: this is intentionally terse and iterative — meant to be a small repo-first experiment rather than long-form productization. Keep feedback lightweight.)
